pr_body:
This PR adds a new (hidden) global flag `--no-pager` to allow disabling the pager in all sub-commands.

closes #3617
pr_comments: +1 for making it a global flag. It would also be great if it supported the short option of `-P` like [`git`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git#Documentation/git.txt--P) does.

> I would much more prefer to see it as a global flag. You can add one to PersistentFlags on the root command (NewCmdRoot()) and add a PersistentPreRun hook that reads the value of the flag and calls f.IOStreams.SetPager() accordingly.

Totally missed that, thanks!

Adding it to `NewCmdRoot` will make `gh` show the flag in commands that doesn't even use the pager, what do you think about moving this functionality to its own file (like [repo_override](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmdutil/repo_override.go)) and then enable it per subcommand? 

> It would also be great if it supported the short option of -P like git does.

@mgaffney I avoided adding a shorthand since IMO it's not something users will commonly use (I guess most will just alias it) and also to leave `-P` short flag free to use in some future command. What do you think @mislav ?

> Adding it to `NewCmdRoot` will make `gh` show the flag in commands that doesn't even use the pager, what do you think about moving this functionality to its own file (like [repo_override](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmdutil/repo_override.go)) and then enable it per subcommand?

That sounds great to me! Good point about `--no-pager` being confusing to see in help of commands that don't make use of a pager at all. 👍 

An alternative could be to still add `--no-pager` as a global flag on root, but mark it as hidden. That way it doesn't show up in help text anywhere, but we could still separately point out that it exists. You are free to choose an approach that feels right to you. Note that we are much more keen on accepting PRs with small diffs than those with large ones. 👌 

> and also to leave `-P` short flag free to use in some future command.

I agree that "global" flags should not have shorthands so that the shorthand can be used for something else in a command. Right now we don't use `-P` for anything, but we might want to in the future.

@cristiand391 Can you confirm that the added PersistentPreRun block doesn't conflict with this one added for the purpose of `-R/--repo` flag (or GH_REPO environment variable) override? https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/dee89a1b6a7a346eb5109f5c6b798ecfa7702f25/pkg/cmdutil/repo_override.go#L13-L13

@mislav I noticed that exactly after I force-pushed (sorry), that's why I marked this PR as draft 👍🏾.
Will update later today.

I've manually tested the new flag and it works on both sub-commands that set their own PersistentPreRun hook and those who don't (like `api`, `gist`, etc).

Should I add a test for this flag?

issue_context.title: Allow changing or disabling the pager per single invocation
issue_context.body:
> Still no `--no-pager` flag, which means I can't disable the pager for some of my aliases
 
_Originally posted by @maelvls in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/528#issuecomment-837996549_

We should support a `--no-pager` flag that disables the pager even if one was set via config file or environment variable.
comments:
I am a bit late to this issue but I would like to propose an alternative solution to the `--no-pager` flag, and that is to increase the precedence of the `GH_PAGER` environment variable that we already support. The new precedence order would be 
`GH_PAGER` (if set), pager configuration setting, and finally `PAGER` environment variable. This would allow users to unset the pager on a per invocation basis while also not introducing any new complexities to how we handle pagers. The only gotcha here is that we need to be able to determine when the environment variable is explicitly set to nothing (`GH_PAGER=""`)  vs when it is just unset in the environment (`GH_PAGER=` ).

I like the idea of GH_PAGER being able to override the `gh config set pager` setting. That way one could either unset the pager (`GH_PAGER="" gh some-command`), set it to `GH_PAGER=cat` (effectively meaning no pager), or set it to another pager program for this invocation only. Right now there isn't a way to override the default pager with a different pager.

@cristiand391 What do you think? Unfortunately, if we went this direction with GH_PAGER, I would argue that we do not also need a flag that serves the same purpose.

@mislav I like this idea!
I've tried implementing it and works as expected (you can even using it in aliases by doing:
`gh alias set --shell diff 'GH_PAGER=delta gh pr diff'`).

Agree that if this is implemented another flag would be redundant.


> The only gotcha here is that we need to be able to determine when the environment variable is explicitly set to nothing (GH_PAGER="") vs when it is just unset in the environment (GH_PAGER= ).

@samcoe [os.LookupEnv](https://pkg.go.dev/os#LookupEnv) allows you do that.

Since there's no need to add another flag, should I open another PR for this?
@cristiand391 Yes, if you don't mind, since this is an entirely different solution, I would like to see a new PR for this. Thank you! 🙇

This has been closed, but #3789 which closed it doesn't seem to address this. I am still unable to `gh issue list > issues.txt` or do any other pipe operation, and I assume this has to do with PAGER or something.

I've tried setting `PAGER` and `GH_PAGER` to various values, but no luck.
A workaround is to set `$PAGER` to empty just for the command you are running: `PAGER= gh release view v1.0.3 --json name,isDraft`

Setting `GH_PAGER=` (to empty) works like a charm.

```bash
~ GH_REPO=cli/cli GH_PAGER= gh release list -L 1 --exclude-drafts --exclude-pre-releases --json tagName -q '.[].tagName'
v2.61.0
```

review_comments: This is needed in order to execute rootCmd's PersistentPreRun hook on all sub-commands that use `EnableRepoOverride` to set their own hook, see https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1198.
